content: Is there a way in VSCode to not immediately start running the entire rest of the file after every individual keystroke I input? It seems to take longer to elaborate the file if it's after some typing, compared to if I paste in the exact same text, and I think the reason is that it's running the whole file after every keystroke when I type stuff in manually. So instead I would like it to wait a bit, say half a second, to make sure I'm done typing before it starts running the rest of the file, and this way it's hopefully not so laggy either since it's not elaborating the 500 lines below my cursor every time I type a letter.
You can write #exit directly below the theorem you are proving to stop Lean from checking the rest of the file, but I guess your question is specifically about keystrokes
yes I can write #exit but I'm not sure about in the middle of a theorem and it's still elaborating every time I type a letter and it's still slow
